description: Mercimek Corbasi is a beloved Turkish red lentil soup, known for its vibrant color and comforting flavor. This classic recipe features simple ingredients transformed into a creamy, hearty, and incredibly satisfying dish. It's often served as a starter but is substantial enough to be a light meal on its own, perfect for any time of year.

instructions.title: Rinse the Lentils
instructions.text: Begin by thoroughly rinsing the red lentils under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any impurities and helps prevent the soup from becoming cloudy. Drain the rinsed lentils well and set aside.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for about 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it becomes soft and translucent. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.

instructions.title: Build the Flavor Base
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato paste, sweet paprika, dried mint, and cumin with the softened onions and garlic. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, allowing the spices to toast and release their aromas. This step deepens the overall flavor profile of the soup.

instructions.title: Combine and Simmer
instructions.text: Add the rinsed and drained red lentils to the pot, along with the chicken or vegetable broth and water. Stir everything together. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the red lentils are very tender and have broken down.

instructions.title: Blend to Smoothness
instructions.text: Carefully remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup directly in the pot until it reaches a smooth, creamy consistency. If you do not have an immersion blender, you can carefully transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender, blend, and then return it to the pot. Be cautious when blending hot liquids.

instructions.title: Season and Finish
instructions.text: Return the pot to low heat. Season the soup generously with salt and black pepper to taste. If the soup is too thick for your preference, you can add a little more hot water or broth to reach the desired consistency. Let it gently simmer for another 5 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chili Butter (Optional)
instructions.text: While the soup is simmering, if you choose to add the traditional Turkish chili butter topping, melt the butter in a small pan over low heat. Add the red pepper flakes (Pul Biber) and a tiny pinch of dried mint to the melted butter. Cook for about 1 minute until the butter is fragrant and the flakes are lightly toasted. Be careful not to burn the butter.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into individual serving bowls. Drizzle each serving with a spoonful of the prepared chili butter (if using) and serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side. A squeeze of lemon juice truly brightens the soup's flavor.

tips: For a richer flavor, use homemade chicken broth. If making it vegetarian, ensure your vegetable broth is high quality.
The traditional Turkish topping, known as 'nane-pul biberli yag,' is crucial for authentic taste. Do not skip the dried mint and red pepper flakes in butter.

Mercimek Corbasi tastes even better the next day. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop, adding a splash of water or broth if needed.
article:
Dive into the heart of Turkish comfort food with a bowl of Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup. This vibrant, flavourful, and incredibly nourishing soup is a cornerstone of Turkish cuisine, beloved for its simplicity, heartwarming taste, and universal appeal. Whether you're seeking a quick, healthy meal or a comforting starter to a grand feast, Mercimek Corbasi delivers a taste of authentic Turkish warmth right to your table. Its beautiful reddish-orange hue, silky smooth texture, and aromatic spice blend make it an irresistible choice, cementing its status as one of the most cherished Turkish soups and stews.

## What is Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup?

Mercimek Corbasi, pronounced "mer-jee-mek chor-ba-suh," literally translates to "lentil soup." It is specifically a red lentil soup, distinguished by its characteristic creamy texture and often bright, inviting colour. This staple soup is a testament to the simplicity and richness of Turkish culinary traditions, often served as a starter at almost every meal, from casual family dinners to formal gatherings. At its heart, Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup is a humble dish made from readily available ingredients, yet it yields a complex and deeply satisfying flavour profile.

The soup's foundation is red lentils, known for their quick cooking time and ability to break down into a smooth consistency. These are typically simmered with aromatic vegetables like onions and garlic, often enriched with tomato paste, and seasoned with a blend of spices that commonly includes dried mint, red pepper flakes (pul biber), and sometimes a touch of paprika. The magic happens when these ingredients meld together, creating a harmonious blend of earthy, savoury, and slightly tangy notes, often brightened with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice just before serving. It’s a dish that embodies the very essence of home cooking – nourishing, comforting, and utterly delicious.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting the perfect Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup requires a handful of simple, wholesome ingredients. The beauty lies in their quality and how they come together.

*   **Red Lentils:** The star of the show. Ensure they are fresh and clean. Rinsing them thoroughly before cooking is crucial to remove any dust or debris.
*   **Onion & Garlic:** The aromatic base. Finely chopped, they provide depth and a sweet, savoury foundation.
*   **Tomato Paste (Salça):** A key ingredient in Turkish cooking. It adds a concentrated umami flavour and contributes to the soup's rich colour. Look for good quality, concentrated tomato paste.
*   **Butter (Tereyağı) or Olive Oil:** Used for sautéing the aromatics and for creating the flavourful "burnt butter" (nane yağı) topping. Butter adds a richer, more traditional flavour, but olive oil is a great alternative for a lighter or vegan version.
*   **Dried Mint (Kuru Nane):** Indispensable for the authentic Turkish flavour. It's often bloomed in the hot butter/oil for the topping, releasing its fragrant oils.
*   **Red Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber or Maras Biber):** Adds a mild warmth and a beautiful red speckle. Adjust the quantity to your spice preference. Smoked paprika can also be used for depth.
*   **Water or Vegetable Broth:** The liquid base. Broth will add more flavour, but water is perfectly acceptable and traditional.
*   **Salt & Black Pepper:** To season the soup to perfection.
*   **Lemon Wedges:** Essential for serving, providing a bright, tangy counterpoint that elevates all the other flavours.

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Making Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup is surprisingly straightforward. Follow these steps for a delicious, authentic result:

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Rinse 1 cup of red lentils under cold running water until the water runs clear. Drain well and set aside.
2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt 2 tablespoons of butter or heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat. Add 1 finely chopped medium onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add 2-3 cloves of minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.
3.  **Add Tomato Paste and Spices:** Stir in 1-2 tablespoons of tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly. This helps to deepen its flavour and colour. Add 1 teaspoon of red pepper flakes (or to taste) and ½ teaspoon of dried mint (if not using for topping) and cook for another 30 seconds until fragrant.
4.  **Combine with Lentils and Liquid:** Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot, stir to combine with the aromatics and paste. Pour in 6-7 cups of water or vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a boil.
5.  **Simmer:** Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot partially, and let the soup simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have broken down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
6.  **Blend (Optional but Recommended):** For a smooth, creamy texture, use an immersion blender to blend the soup directly in the pot until silky smooth. If you don't have an immersion blender, carefully transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth. Return it to the pot.
7.  **Season:** Season the soup generously with salt and black pepper to taste. You may need more salt than you think, as lentils absorb a lot of flavour.
8.  **Prepare the Topping (Nane Yağı):** In a small saucepan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium-low heat. Once melted and slightly foamy, add 1-2 teaspoons of dried mint and another ½ teaspoon of red pepper flakes (optional). Swirl for about 30 seconds until the mint becomes fragrant and the butter turns a beautiful reddish hue. Be careful not to burn the mint.
9.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot soup into bowls. Drizzle a spoonful of the aromatic butter topping over each serving. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side, allowing each diner to squeeze in juice to their liking.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Mastering Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup isn't difficult, but a few professional tips can elevate your homemade version from good to absolutely sublime.

*   **Rinse Those Lentils!** This is non-negotiable. Rinsing removes starches and impurities, leading to a cleaner flavour and preventing the soup from becoming too cloudy or gummy.
*   **Sautéing is Key:** Don't rush the initial sautéing of the onions and garlic. Allowing them to soften and sweeten properly lays a crucial flavour base for the entire soup. Cooking the tomato paste for a minute or two also deepens its flavour significantly.
*   **Achieve Silky Smoothness:** While some prefer a slightly chunkier soup, the hallmark of traditional Mercimek Corbasi is its velvety texture. An immersion blender makes this incredibly easy. If using a regular blender, blend in batches and be cautious with hot liquids.
*   **Seasoning is Crucial:** Taste, taste, taste! Lentils absorb a lot of salt, so don't be shy. Adjust salt and pepper as needed after blending. A perfectly seasoned soup sings.
*   **The Lemon is Non-Negotiable:** Seriously, don't skip the lemon. The bright acidity cuts through the richness of the lentils and spices, adding a vital freshness and balance that transforms the soup. It's truly what makes Mercimek Corbasi shine.
*   **Don't Skimp on the Butter Topping:** The "nane yağı" (mint butter) is more than just a garnish; it's an integral part of the flavour profile. The fragrant, slightly nutty butter infused with dried mint and red pepper flakes adds an aromatic richness and visual appeal that completes the dish.

## Serving Suggestions

Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup is traditionally served as a starter, but it's hearty enough to be a light meal on its own, especially when paired with crusty bread.

*   **Lemon Wedges:** As mentioned, these are essential. Always offer them on the side.
*   **Crusty Bread (Ekmek):** A must for dipping and soaking up every last drop of the delicious soup. Turkish bread, pita, or even a good sourdough work wonderfully.
*   **Fresh Herbs:** A sprinkle of fresh parsley or mint adds a burst of colour and freshness.
*   **Extra Red Pepper Flakes:** For those who like a little more heat, a small bowl of pul biber on the side is a welcome addition.
*   **Pickles (Turşu):** In Turkey, it's common to serve soup with a side of mixed pickles, which provide a tangy crunch that contrasts beautifully with the smooth soup.
*   **Alongside Kebabs or Salads:** If serving as part of a larger meal, Mercimek Corbasi pairs well with grilled meats, fresh salads, or rice dishes.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup is perfect as is, there are many ways to adapt it to your taste or dietary needs.

*   **Make it Vegan:** Simply use olive oil instead of butter for sautéing and for the topping. The rest of the ingredients are naturally plant-based. Ensure you use vegetable broth if not using water.
*   **Add Vegetables:** For extra nutrients and flavour, you can add finely diced carrots, celery, or potatoes along with the onions. Add them at the sautéing stage to soften. A handful of fresh spinach can also be stirred in during the last few minutes of cooking.
*   **Spice it Up:** Experiment with other Turkish spices like cumin, sumac, or black pepper. A pinch of cumin can add an extra layer of earthiness.
*   **Different Lentils:** While red lentils are traditional and yield the characteristic smooth texture, you could try yellow lentils for a similar result. Green or brown lentils will hold their shape more and result in a chunkier soup, which is a different, but still delicious, experience.
*   **Creaminess Factor:** For an even creamier soup, some recipes add a splash of milk or cream at the very end, just before serving. This is less traditional but can be a delicious indulgence.
*   **Smoky Flavour:** A pinch of smoked paprika can add a lovely depth and subtle smoky note to the soup.

Whether you're new to Turkish cuisine or a seasoned fan, Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup is a recipe that belongs in your repertoire. Its ease of preparation, wholesome ingredients, and deeply satisfying flavour make it a timeless dish that brings comfort and joy to any table. Enjoy the taste of Turkey, one spoonful at a time!
